title: When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation

visual_explainer.question: After a retrieval fault propagates through later hops, which intervention can still identify the causal hop?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Certified hop faults separate observation from intervention: frozen-hop continuation and downstream regeneration preserve different, imperfect diagnostic signals.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Post-hoc answer-coverage localization and a cross-family trace judge under the same failed traces.

analysis.tldr: AgenticRAG-FP turns failure attribution into an intervention problem by injecting a certified hop fault and rerunning either the frozen hop or its downstream suffix. On one completed Claude/MuSiQue condition, post-hoc coverage loses exact-hop information after propagation while counterfactual probes retain partial signal. The comparison is survivor-, compute-, and harness-dependent.
analysis.problem: An incorrect final answer does not reveal which retrieval hop first caused the failure, because later retrieval and reasoning can heal, amplify, or obscure the original fault.
analysis.core_idea: Inject a known structural or content fault at a specific hop, retain the failing traces, then compare post-hoc coverage/judging with counterfactual frozen-hop continuation and suffix regeneration.
analysis.agent_loop: run multi-hop agent → inject certified fault → observe failure propagation → freeze or regenerate downstream execution → diagnose causal hop
analysis.retrieval_design: The benchmark intervenes on live retrieval trajectories rather than labeling an existing trace after the fact. Exact-hop attribution is conditioned on trajectories that still fail after intervention.
analysis.evidence: In strict dense Claude/MuSiQue, exact-hop coverage is 0.91/0.00/0.00 for hops 1/2/3; the cross-family judge is 0.26/0.25/0.43 and frozen-hop repair 0.51/0.25/0.48. Content-fault suffix regeneration can fall to 0.11 at hop 2.
analysis.why_it_matters: It supplies an executable causal-evaluation design for asking where retrieval failure began, not merely where the final trace looks suspicious.
limitations: Only still-failed trajectories are scored, so depth denominators differ and survivor bias is unavoidable.
The corpus remains clean under content corruption, allowing later retrieval to heal 54–85% of interventions.
Active probes rerun the agent while post-hoc methods do not, so costs are unmatched.
Headline evidence is one model, retriever, dataset, and four-probe budget; several cells are tiny.
No realized token, call, latency, dollar, or total experiment-cost table is reported.
